slides.title: Writing to the Console
slides.content: Console.WriteLine outputs text followed by a new line. Console.Write outputs text without moving to a new line.

exercise.prompt: Which method prints text and moves to the next line?

slides.title: Formatting Output
slides.content: You can embed variables directly in strings using string interpolation with the $ prefix and curly braces.

exercise.prompt: Complete the interpolation syntax to print the age variable: Console.WriteLine($"Age: {_____}");

slides.title: Escape Sequences
slides.content: Escape sequences use a backslash to insert special characters like newlines and tabs into strings.

exercise.prompt: Drag the correct escape sequence to print a tab character: Console.WriteLine("A[?]B");

slides.title: Placeholders and Composite Formatting
slides.content: String.Format and composite formatting use numbered placeholders {0}, {1} to insert values in order.

slides.title: Combining Text and Variables
slides.content: String concatenation joins strings with +. Interpolation is usually cleaner and less error-prone.

exercise.prompt: Write a Console.WriteLine using string interpolation to print: Result: 42
hints: Make sure your code includes the required keywords/elements: $
When run, your code should output: Result: 42

slides.title: Verbatim String Literals
slides.content: Verbatim strings start with @ and preserve whitespace and backslashes. They are useful for file paths.

exercise.prompt: A verbatim string starts with the @ symbol. Complete: string path = @"_____\file.txt";

slides.title: Printing Without Newlines
slides.content: Console.Write stays on the same line. Use Console.WriteLine() only when you want to advance to the next line.

exercise.prompt: Which method keeps the cursor on the same line?

slides.title: Output Review
slides.content: C# offers Write, WriteLine, interpolation, placeholders, escape sequences, and verbatim strings for output.

exercise.prompt: Print an escaped newline followed by a tab: first line, then indented second line.
hints: Make sure your code includes the required keywords/elements: \n, \t
When run, your code should output: First line, 	Second line, Indented

slides.title: Flow Builder: Output
slides.content: Use the Flow Builder to create an output that prints a greeting with a newline.

exercise.prompt: Build a flow that outputs 'Hello, World!' with a newline
